subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm/mempolicy: stop copying state in the interleave paths

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: Reviewer Andrew Morton noted that alloc_pages_bulk_interleave() may cause a division by zero error, citing an external review from Sashiko, and requested further investigation.
reviews.raw_body:
Not very well, it seems.  Sashiko thinks there's a div-by-zero in
alloc_pages_bulk_interleave().

	https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260829015943.1258774-1-gourry@gourry.net

2026-08-29.patch_summary: This patch eliminates unnecessary copies of nodemask and node weights in the interleave paths of the Linux kernel's memory policy module. It achieves this by using SRCU to pin node weights in place, operating directly on pol->nodes for nodemasks, and clamping the walk to a single pass. The changes improve performance but may introduce a small trade-off in distribution accuracy during rebind operations.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), agreed to restructure in v2, but did not provide any technical details or explanation for the change.

reviews.author: Rakie Kim
reviews.summary:
Rakie Kim noted that the patch does not address the case where a node is removed from the system, which would cause the interleave node selectors to fall back to numa_node_id() and potentially return an incorrect result.

Reviewer Rakie Kim agrees that using SRCU to resolve the sleeping-allocation problem is a good approach and suggests continuing in this direction.

Reviewer noted that after the patch, the loop bound no longer matches the mask if it changes between reads, and suggested counting nodes in the weight sum loop like weighted_interleave_nid() does
sentiment_signals: patch does not address edge cases
reviews.raw_body:
Hello Gregory,

Thanks for the series.

On Fri, 28 Aug 2026 21:59:43 -0400 Gregory Price <gourry@gourry.net> wrote:

---

I went through both patches. Resolving the sleeping-allocation
problem with SRCU rather than patching the allocation site, and
removing the copies from the fault path along the way, looks like
the right direction to me.

---

I have a minor comment on this part. After this change, everything
else reads pol->nodes fresh at the point of use - the weight sum
and the walk both look at the current mask. Only nnodes is still
the count from this earlier read. If the mask changes in between,
the loop bound no longer matches the mask the loop is actually
walking, so the walk can stop short of the pages the weight total
planned for. Would it be better to count the nodes in the loop
that sums the weights, the way weighted_interleave_nid() does it
in this patch?

	nnodes = 0;
	for_each_node_mask(node, pol->nodes) {
		weight_total += table ? table[node] : 1;
		nnodes++;
	}

[...snip...]

Thanks again for your time.

Rakie Kim

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author responded to Rakie Kim's feedback, stating that widening the SRCU window to include the cpuset cookie does not fix anything and may even be counterproductive by calculating weight totals unnecessarily.
sentiment_signals: questions the effectiveness of proposed solution
